scope_entries.finding: login users now carry pi 0.85.0 under ~/.local/share/pi-node/node-v22.23.2-linux-arm64 (PATH line in .bashrc, interactive shells only; pi's shebang needs that node on PATH) and qwen on PATH — thor 0.22.0, orin 0.23.0 (drift against unix-user.sh's 0.22.0 pin); neither host has ~/.pi/agent/settings.json or models.json, so pi has no provider yet; orin :8000 answers 401 (keyed gateway, model-gear-vllm-associate + gateway containers up) so orin does serve a local lobe; engine accounts still hold only codex

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: deploy/prod/install-secrets.sh + culture-nodes-qwen-developer.service
scope_entries.finding: the account-side secret copy is codex-only today (install_codex_account_env, line 533); the qwen unit loads %h/.culture-nodes/bridge-push.env, so a new account without that step serves but cannot push

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: scripts/lint-all.sh, tests/test_lint_all.py::test_it_lists_exactly_the_three_jobs, CLAUDE.md lint section
scope_entries.finding: the three-job scope is pinned by a test and documented as deliberate; c11 widens it, so the pin, the doc sentence and the codex-vs-claude-code invocation difference must be decided together

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / unstated-assumptions lens: adapters/qwen/acp/gate.py + c9/c16 interplay
scope_entries.finding: c9 admits yolo 'when the bridge runs as culture-qwen' and spark's bridge is also culture-qwen; the code is shared, the mode is per-dispatch — recorded so c16 is not read as pinning spark to the old revision

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / counter-evidence probe: POST thor:8000/v1/chat/completions (developer role, tools, stream usage) 2026-09-04
scope_entries.finding: the served Qwen3.8 accepts the developer role (200, usage with reasoning_tokens), returns real tool_calls with finish_reason=tool_calls under tool_choice=auto, and emits a usage chunk with stream_options.include_usage — so pi's openai-completions provider needs no compat.supportsDeveloperRole override and both harnesses' tool loops have a working backend; culture-codex@orin reaches thor:8000 by name and by IP (200)

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / unstated-assumptions lens: pi package.json (0.84.2 on spark) vs pi 0.85.0 on thor/orin; unix-user.sh pins
scope_entries.finding: two pi versions and two qwen versions are now on the fleet; the spec read 0.84.2's docs and 0.85.0's --help (same json/rpc/print/no-session/no-extensions/no-skills/no-context-files/tools flags) — the event schema itself was not re-read for 0.85.0

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / failure-modes lens: pi with no provider (thor/orin have no ~/.pi/agent/models.json today), deploy/prod/codex-preflight.sh
scope_entries.finding: pi's exit behaviour with an unconfigured provider was not probed; codex has a deploy-time non-billable preflight and pi has none — the first evidence would otherwise be a failed billable run

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / observability lens: adapters/qwen state_dir/acp-transcripts (README), pi docs/json.md
scope_entries.finding: the qwen README calls the transcript 'the first thing to read when a dispatch behaves oddly'; pi's print mode streams the equivalent to stdout and the bridge must keep it or it is gone; process-group kill is unverified for pi's bash tool

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / operations lens: issue #289 (open) + deploy.sh account lanes
scope_entries.finding: deploy.sh exits 0 when the account provision lane refuses the actor checkout; the two new lanes per host inherit that defect, so a refused qwen/pi provision on thor or orin would look green — a plan-side risk to land with devague plan risk, not a spec change

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / concurrency lens: ADR 0013 (bridges single-threaded), issue #181, thor:8000 as the one backend
scope_entries.finding: each bridge runs one session at a time, so four new actors add at most four concurrent sessions against thor's vLLM beside colleague and spark's own load; per-actor ceilings are approximate (#181); no measurement of thor's concurrent-session capacity exists — residual, parked

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security lens: docs/deviations/2026-08-29-agents-as-os-users.md 'LAN reachability, unexamined' (line 196)
scope_entries.finding: an engine account reaches every LAN service; the deviation record says reachability is not access (no DB credential, API needs the actor token) and explicitly does not claim harmlessness; two more no-approval harnesses per host widen what an injected prompt can try, not what it can reach — residual, parked

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / reversibility lens: register-actor.sh, internal/api actor rows (append-only), unix-user.sh rollback pair
scope_entries.finding: there is no deregister/retire verb: stopping a broken pi or qwen actor means stopping its unit (dispatches then fail as connection refused) and, for the account, the documented rollback pair; a registration row cannot be withdrawn — parked as a question of operator practice, not a spec change

obligations.behavior: pi and qwen are dispatchable actors on thor/orin; a run records which harness+model served it
obligations.source_text: Culture Nodes supports Pi and Qwen Code as actors again: each runs as its own OS account on thor and orin through the existing actor contract, a workflow can name any of them as a node's actor, and a run records which harness and model served it — so a flow that sends the same request through several actors can compare them

obligations.behavior: the four actors are registered, healthy, and reachable by nodes-op assign; a starved/no-write session reports a distinct outcome
obligations.source_text: company/pi-thor, pi-orin, qwen-thor and qwen-orin are registered, healthy actors that nodes-op.sh assign and any workflow definition can target like codex-thor today; each actor row carries harness=, model= and model_endpoint=; a permission-starved or no-write session reports a distinct outcome, never completed

obligations.behavior: one real pi run and one real qwen run each complete with a ledgered run; the conformance kit passes; deploy installs both bridges idempotently
obligations.source_text: one real dispatch to a pi actor and one to a qwen actor on thor or orin each complete with a ledgered run and a handover ref; the conformance kit passes against the fake-backed pi and qwen bridges in CI; deploy.sh thor|orin installs both bridges into their accounts idempotently

obligations.behavior: the pi bridge drives pi --mode json, shared core byte-identical to qwen, offline tests green
obligations.source_text: a sixth adapter, adapters/pi (pi-bridge), drives @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.2 as one pi process per invocation over its native JSONL surface (--mode json print run, or --mode rpc) and ports the byte-identical core (preflight.py, dialin.py, deployment.py, reap.py) from the qwen sibling unchanged

obligations.behavior: the example fans one instruction to a run-time actor list and joins per-actor outcomes; compiles + fixture-runs
obligations.source_text: an example workflow under examples/ (harness-compare) fans one request to a list of actors chosen at run time and joins their results, so comparing harnesses is a flow an operator can run, not a property every dispatch must have; it is a possibility the design keeps open, and running it is optional

obligations.behavior: a permission-cancelled qwen session reports permission_blocked and an empty workspace-write reports no_changes, never completed; yolo admitted
obligations.source_text: issue #228 is answered, not patched around: under an engine account the confinement IS the account (no sudo, no docker group, 750 home — docs/deviations/2026-08-29-agents-as-os-users.md), which is exactly the boundary #228 item 3 said was missing, so the qwen bridge admits yolo (wire.ACP_MODES) when the bridge runs as culture-qwen, and the pi bridge — which has no permission prompt at all (docs/security.md: no built-in sandbox, tools run as the process user) — is admitted on the same reasoning; both bridges still report a permission-cancelled or empty-write session as a distinct outcome, never completed (#228 items 1 and 2)
